title: Organizational Architecture Baseline - Quick Commerce Operations
citation: Gulick, L., & Urwick, L. (Eds.). (1937). Papers on the Science of Administration. Institute of Public Administration, New York.

P.name: Planning
P.role: Demand forecasting, algorithmic SKU placement, dark-store geo-clustering

O.name: Organizing
O.role: Hub-and-spoke dark store networks, micro-fulfillment station layouts

S.name: Staffing
S.role: Picker and packer onboarding, 50,000+ rider fleet gig management

D.name: Directing
D.role: Automated dispatch engines, dynamic ETA updates, rider route guidance

CO.name: Coordinating
CO.role: FMCG vendor deliveries, cold-chain replenishment, 3-minute picking SLA

R.name: Reporting
R.role: Real-time dark store telemetry, out-of-stock (OOS) rates, rider idle time

B.name: Budgeting
B.role: Dark store lease capex, rider surge incentives, customer CAC burn

mechanistic.name: Mechanistic Bureaucracy (Taylor / Weber)
mechanistic.characteristics: High formalization, specialized roles, high centralization, tall hierarchy, rigid SLAs.
mechanistic.pros: Flawless operational consistency, minimal picking errors, strict inventory control.
mechanistic.cons: Slow innovation, rider alienation, inability to respond rapidly to local neighborhood shifts.

organic.name: Organic Agile Network (Burns & Stalker / Contingency)
organic.characteristics: Low formalization, decentralized decision rights, broad span of control, flat hierarchy.
organic.pros: Rapid hyper-local experimentation (Zepto Cafe, fresh flower delivery), agile rider redeployment.
organic.cons: Higher coordination overhead, potential shrinkage/pilferage, inconsistent customer service.
